name: Far left
summary: Far-left politics is the family of anti-capitalist ideologies to the left of the mainstream left, covering communism, anarchism, other revolutionary socialisms and Maoism. Scholarship defines it by rejection of capitalism and neoliberalism and a push for economic equality through collective ownership, planning and redistribution, with strands that differ sharply on the state, democracy, immigration and violence.
scope: The far left as defined in open radical-left scholarship (Fagerholm 2017, Rooduijn et al. 2017, Jacot et al. 2021, Kopyciok and Silver 2021, Krüsselmann and Weggemans 2023): the party family and ideological current that rejects capitalism and seeks economic equality through collective ownership and redistribution, with anarchist, communist, Maoist and new-left strands. Texts of Marx and the Stanford entries on Marx and anarchism are not used for answers because no defining source ties them to the far left; they belong to communism and anarchism, audited separately. Where the scholarship says only that strands differ, the answer is null.

notes: Heterogeneous umbrella. In the rules 7 pass, answers resting on Wikipedia, the Communist Manifesto, the Civil War in France and the Stanford entries on Marx and anarchism were nulled, because no defining source for the far left ties those texts to it (communism and anarchism are audited separately). Searched: open scholarship on the radical left and far left (OpenAlex open-access search, the sources Wikipedia cites; Tandfonline and Springer copies refused access and were not used); themes covered: economy, ownership, equality, state and democracy, nationalism and immigration, violence. These sources describe party families and voters, so few statements are settled. Many answers are null on that evidence.
